discussion_comments.comment_body: Yes this is true. I reverted this now. I thought I hadn't committed it.

I'd actually noticed earlier we're starting to accumulate a few docker compose files. personally I feel like the optimal amount to have is 2: one for running the whole stack locally via docker compose, with default images, and the other for running the infra components locally and running a dev server separately.

I think `docker/docker-compose.yml` and  `docker/docker-compose-local.yml`/`docker/docker-compose-dev.yml` are intended to be those files (respectively), maybe we could update those if theres an issue with them instead of adding a new one?

I think it would be nice to DRY up our docker compose files. maybe we can have like a `docker/docker-compose.infra.yml` that contains the infra components like pg and minio etc. and then a `docker/docker-compose.helicone.yml` that contains helicone software like the workers and the web. 

then if ur developing locally you can do `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.infra.yml up -d` but if you want to run the entire stack you can do `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.infra.yml -f docker/docker-compose.helicone.yml up -d` and combine the compose files.

Another way to do it is to have a single docker compose file and use the `--profile` arg eg `docker compose up -d` would start the infra and `docker compose --profile include-helicone up -d` would start the entire stack

this should make them a lot more maintainable
I agree, can we scope this into a different ticket? @devinat1 can you fast follow with DRYing up our docker compose files next week?
Agreed, I have made a separate ticket for this (https://linear.app/helicone/issue/ENG-1860/dry-the-docker-compose-files) since regressions may arise upon DRYing up the compose files.
I have removed docker-compose-stateless.yml since I was using it just to test ECR (doesn't add new functionality)
